questions.question: In the dynamic lot-size model, $y_i$ is the order, $x_i$ the starting stock and $D_i$ the demand of period $i$, with $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i\ge0$. The zero-inventory ordering property says that, with no shortages or lead time, nonincreasing marginal production and holding costs and $x_1=0$, some optimal policy has $y_ix_i=0$ for all $i$. What does $y_ix_i=0$ require in each period $i$?
options: The order $y_i$ equals the demand $D_i$ of that period
No order is placed, or the period starts with no stock
The stock $x_{i+1}$ left at the end of period $i$ is zero
Stock and order are never zero in the same period

questions.question: A dynamic lot-size plan with zero final stock satisfies $y_ix_i=0$ in every period ($y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock, $D_i$ demand of period $i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$). Period $i$ orders, and the next positive order is in period $t+1>i$. What is $y_i$?
options: $D_i$
$D_i+\dots+D_{t+1}$
$D_i+\dots+D_t$
$D_i+\dots+D_n$

questions.question: The zero-inventory ordering property for the uncapacitated dynamic lot-size model ($y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock in period $i$) guarantees an optimal policy with $y_ix_i=0$ for all $i$. Which assumption is part of its statement?
options: Nonincreasing marginal production and holding costs
Demand that stays the same in every period
A setup cost that is equal across all periods
A positive initial stock $x_1>0$ in the first period

questions.question: A four-period dynamic lot-size problem with demands $D=(30,20,40,10)$ meets the assumptions of the zero-inventory ordering property, so some optimal policy has $y_ix_i=0$ for all $i$ ($y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock and $D_i$ demand in period $i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$). If period 2 starts with $x_2=0$, which set lists every positive order $y_2$ such a policy can use?

A dynamic lot-size problem has initial stock $x_1=25$ and demands $D=(10,30,20)$. The course nets positive initial stock before applying the zero-inventory ordering property. Which net demands remain?

A dynamic lot-size problem has demands $D=(15,25,10,30)$ and $x_1=0$ ($y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock and $D_i$ demand in period $i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$). Which order plan violates the zero-inventory condition $y_ix_i=0$?

A four-period dynamic lot-size problem has positive demand in every period, $x_1=0$ and zero final stock, and only order plans with $y_ix_i=0$ in every period are considered ($y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock and $D_i$ demand in period $i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$). How many such plans are there?

A forward recursion for the $n$-period dynamic lot-size model uses the zero-inventory ordering property: some optimal policy orders only when the starting stock is zero ($y_ix_i=0$; $y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock, $D_i$ demand). Period $i$ starts with $x_i=0$. How many positive orders $y_i$ must be compared?
options: $D_i+\dots+D_n$, one per unit of remaining demand
$n$, one per period of the whole horizon
$n-i+1$, one per possible last covered period
$2^{n-i}$, one per pattern of later orders

questions.question: An order plan for demands $D_1,\dots,D_n$ orders only in periods that start with zero stock (so $y_ix_i=0$, where $y_i$ is the order and $x_i$ the starting stock of period $i$) and ends with zero stock. Which values can a starting stock $x_i$ take?
options: 0 or a total $D_i+\dots+D_t$, $t\ge i$
Any integer from 0 up to $D_i+\dots+D_n$
Only 0, since stock is never carried
0 or one later demand $D_t$ with $t\ge i$

questions.question: The zero-inventory ordering property guarantees, under its assumptions, that some optimal dynamic lot-size policy has $y_ix_i=0$ in every period ($y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock). A particular feasible plan satisfies $y_ix_i=0$ in every period. What follows about its cost?
options: It is optimal, as only optimal plans have this form
It is optimal provided that it orders in period 1
It costs at most as much as ordering every period
Nothing beyond feasibility; costs must be compared

questions.question: A dynamic lot-size problem meeting the property's assumptions has demands $D=(30,20,40,10)$, $x_1=0$, setup cost 45 per order and holding cost 1 per unit of end-of-period stock; the constant unit price is left out. Comparing plans that order only at zero stock, which plan is optimal?

A dynamic lot-size problem has initial stock $x_1=40$ and demands $D=(15,35,20,25)$. After netting the stock as the course does, the zero-inventory ordering property is applied. When is the first positive order placed, and which sizes are its candidates?
options: Period 2, of size 35, 55 or 80
Period 1, of size 15, 50, 70 or 95
Period 3, of size 20 or 45
Period 2, of size 10, 30 or 55

questions.question: A dynamic lot-size problem has demands $D=(20,30,10)$, $x_1=0$, setup cost 50 per order and holding cost 1 per unit of end stock $x_{i+1}$. The plan $(30,30,0)$ orders in period 2 although $x_2=10$. Moving those 10 units into the period-2 order gives $(20,40,0)$. By how much does setup plus holding cost fall?

A dynamic lot-size problem meets every assumption of the zero-inventory ordering property, which guarantees an optimal policy with $y_ix_i=0$ for all $i$ ($y_i$ order, $x_i$ starting stock and $D_i$ demand in period $i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$). Full dynamic programming returns an optimal plan that orders in a period with positive starting stock. What follows?
options: The assumptions must fail, as every optimum has $y_ix_i=0$
The computation is wrong, as such a plan cannot be optimal
Nothing is wrong; a tied optimum with $y_ix_i=0$ exists
The property only constrains the final period's order

questions.question: The zero-inventory ordering property assumes nonincreasing marginal production costs. For an order of $y>0$ units, which variable ordering cost $c(y)$ meets this assumption?
options: $c(y)=10\sqrt y$

questions.question: Two periods have demands $D=(5,15)$, $x_1=0$ and zero final stock, setup cost 10 per order, holding cost 1 per unit of end stock $x_2$, and variable ordering cost $c(y)=y^2$ for an order of $y$ units. Which order plan has the lowest total cost?
